title: Halting on an invalid field
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $f$ and $bits$ be a Boolean and a bit vector of length equal to the number of selector types of $M$. For every Boolean word $rest$, natural number $p$, and Boolean words $w_C,w_O$, suppose $1\le p$, $p+|rest|=|y|+1$, the suffix of $y$ beginning at position $p-1$ is $rest$, and reading a field from $rest$ returns no result. Then, starting the tabulating machine for $M$ in state $fA(f,bits)$ at input position $\min(p,|y|+1)$ with auxiliary words $[],w_C,w_O$, there is a time $s\le |rest|+1$ at which it has halted and its output is exactly $[\mathrm{false}]$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Boolean Turing machine
$bits$ has length equal to the number of selector types of $M$
the suffix of $y$ from position $p-1$ is $rest$
reading a field from $rest$ returns no result
